newsitem.title: USA: Flurry of US corporate bond new issues to hit mart.
newsitem.headline: Flurry of US corporate bond new issues to hit mart.

text.p: A flurry of investment-grade and high-yield U.S. corporate bond deals are expected to be sold to investors by the end of the week, market sources said.
Syndicate officials said close to $3 billion in new high-grade bonds and slightly over $1 billion in new junk bonds are likely to be sold over on Thursday and Friday.
Shortly after 1000EDT/1400GMT, a Salomon Brothers Inc-led syndicate launched a $2.05 billion debt offering for CSX Corp, market sources said.
The deal, which is said to be meeting with good market demand, is expected to price later on Thursday, they said.

In the high-yield market, Allied Waste Industries Inc is expected to sell $240 million senior subordinated notes in 144a offering via Goldman Sachs & Co and Merrill Lynch & Co Inc on Thursday, market sources said.
Price talk on the deal, which is rated CAA/B-plus, is 200 basis points over comparable Treasuries, they said.
Syndicate officials said a more stable Treasury market has improved overall conditions for issuance of both high-grade and junk bonds.
In the high-yield market, a return of cash inflows into junk bond mutual funds has also improved the market tone, they said.
Market sources said other high-yield offerings expected to hit the market on Thursday are:
-CMS Energy Corp's $300 million offering of five-year senior notes via Morgan Stanley & Co.
-HCC Industry Inc's $85 million 144a offering of 10-year senior notes via Credit Suisse First Boston.
-Colorado Prime Corp's $100 million 144a offering of 10-year senior notes via JP Morgan Securities Corp.
Market sources said other investment-grade deals expected to be priced on Thursday are:

-Sun Life Assurance Co of Canada's $500 million 144a offering of perpetual step-up capital units, rated AA2/AA, via Merrill Lynch & Co. The units, which will not have registration rights, will be noncallable for 10 years, sources said. Price talk was not available.
-Comdisco Inc's $250 million offering of BAA1/BBB-plus-rated, two-year notes via Salomon Brothers. Price talk is around 35 basis points over Treasuries, market sources said.
